title: How Are LLMs Mitigating Stereotyping Harms? Learning from Search Engine Studies

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at various age groups (e.g., boomers, teenagers) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.

Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at gender and gender identity groups (e.g., women, transgenders) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.

Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at lifestyle and socioeconomic groups (e.g., homeless people, poor people, rich people) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.

Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at political and politicised groups (e.g., conservatives, socialists, immigrants) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.

Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at peoples and ethnicities (e.g., Asians, Black people, White people, including intersectional identities) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.
Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at various nationalities and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.

Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at religious groups (e.g., Atheists, Jews, Muslims, Christians) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.

Evaluating open-ended LLM generations using autocomplete-style prompts directed at sexual orientation groups (e.g., bisexual people, gay men, lesbians, queer people) and scoring the responses based on refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard.
